format: Parser oracle. tickets: one full TicketMeta per ticket file (legacyRule is null for migrated files). items, links, refs, textRefs are keyed by docs-relative path; line numbers are 1-based file lines and endLine is the last non-blank line of an item; resolved objects follow the Resolved shape in docs/assets/04-parser-contract-draft.md.

decisions.D2: Rule 1 narrowed: superseded only when text starts with "superseded" or contains "superseded by NN"
decisions.D3: "merged" without "not" wins over rule 4; "Not merged ... built on ..." is in-review
decisions.D4: waiting_on inferred for blocked legacy tickets from person words; Type token wins; never for done/dropped/superseded
decisions.D5: fallback stretches typography and word order only; unblocked, parked, pending stay unknown
decisions.D6: Open questions hides closed tickets by default (see viewDefaults)
decisions.D7: the other 16 ambiguities follow the draft

viewDefaults.note: D6: Q items in done, dropped or superseded tickets are hidden from Open questions, with a toggle. The parser indexes all of them.

ambiguities.case: modules/cash-handling-workflow/issues/19 and 20: 'Resolved (superseded by the D3 amendment)', 'Dropped — superseded by 30'
ambiguities.chosen: Rule 1 matches only when the text starts with "superseded" or contains "superseded by NN". 19 is done (rule 6); 12 and 20 stay superseded (rule 1).
ambiguities.why: Rules run in order and rule 1 matches 'superseded' anywhere, so rule 1 beats rules 2 and 6. A resolved ticket that merely mentions a superseded clause is wrongly marked superseded. Suggest anchoring rule 1 to the start or to 'superseded by'.

ambiguities.case: legacy superseded tickets have no superseded_by
ambiguities.chosen: Legacy superseded tickets get superseded_by from "superseded by NN": 12 is "45", 20 is "30".
ambiguities.why: The fallback gives only a status. 'superseded by 45' could be parsed into a ref but the table does not say so. The STATUS_SHAPE warning (superseded with no superseded_by) would fire on every legacy file, so the check must skip legacy.
ambiguities.was: expected has no superseded_by field for legacy files

ambiguities.case: cash-handling-workflow/issues/11: 'Won’t do' with a curly apostrophe
ambiguities.chosen: Curly quotes are normalised before matching. 11 is dropped (rule 2).
ambiguities.why: The pattern uses an ASCII apostrophe. Real files typed in editors with smart quotes would miss rule 2 and fall to unknown. Suggest normalising U+2019 to ' before matching.

ambiguities.case: issues/21: 'Blocked — built on branch claude/ocm-hook, awaiting DBA'
ambiguities.chosen: 21 stays blocked (rule 3 before rule 4).
ambiguities.why: Rule 3 comes before rule 4. Reads right here. No conflict found in the other direction.

ambiguities.case: issues/13 'blocked on DBA' and cloud-migration/08 'blocked on infra'
ambiguities.chosen: waiting_on is inferred from person words (owner, client, dba, infra, ops) in the status text of a blocked legacy ticket. 21 is dba, cloud-migration 08 is infra. 13 stays ops because the Type token wins. Never set when status is done, dropped or superseded.
ambiguities.why: The fallback table does not extract waiting_on. The viewer's Waiting-on view will miss legacy tickets. Only the '+ ops' Type token sets waiting_on (see A9).
ambiguities.was: status blocked, waiting_on not derived from the status text

ambiguities.case: issues/39: 'Built on claude/ocm-ledger, merged to dev'
ambiguities.chosen: "merged" without a preceding "not" means done, even with a branch name. 39 is done (rule 6).
ambiguities.why: Rule 4 fires on 'on claude/' even though the text says merged. Rule 4 has no negative check for 'merged'. Real data likely has this: the branch name stays in the text after the merge.

ambiguities.case: issues/38: 'Not merged — built on claude/ocm-x'
ambiguities.chosen: "Not merged — built on ..." means in-review (rule 4). 38 is in-review.
ambiguities.why: Rule 4 needs the text to start with 'built', so the reversed order falls through every rule. Arguably should be in-review.

ambiguities.case: issues/31: 'Done (not merged to dev yet)'
ambiguities.chosen: 31 stays done (first word wins).
ambiguities.why: 'not merged' only counts for text starting with 'built'. Contradictory text is taken at its first word.

ambiguities.case: issues/13 'task + ops'
ambiguities.chosen: Non-enum Type tokens are dropped; a person token in Type sets waiting_on and wins over the status text. It is set only while the ticket is not done, dropped or superseded.
ambiguities.why: The generic rule 'a + b becomes [a, b]' would give [task, ops], and ops is not in the type enum. Handoff section 2 says it becomes task + waiting_on ops. Chosen: tokens not in the type enum are dropped, and a token in the waiting_on enum sets waiting_on. This is applied for any status, while the handoff says 'while the ops step is open'; a done ticket would still show waiting_on ops.

ambiguities.case: missing Type line, or Type with unknown token
ambiguities.chosen: Missing Type or unknown token gives type [] plus a warning naming the token. Case-insensitive.
ambiguities.why: No rule for a missing Type. Case is ignored: 'Build' becomes build (issues/25).

ambiguities.case: issues/34 (no Status line) and 35 ('✅' only, empty after stripping)
ambiguities.chosen: 34 and 35 are unknown (rule 8) with status_note null.
ambiguities.why: Rule 8 says 'anything else', so an absent or empty status is unknown. No status_note is set.

ambiguities.case: issues/36 'Unblocked — ready to build'; 37 'Open (dropped from sprint 4)'
ambiguities.chosen: 36 stays unknown (no new vocabulary, raw text kept). 37 is open (rule 7).
ambiguities.why: '^blocked' does not match 'unblocked', so 36 falls to unknown even though it means ready. Rule 2 needs the word at the start, so 37 is open. Both follow the rules literally.

ambiguities.case: issues/08 '**Status:** in progress' and 09 'Status: `open`'
ambiguities.chosen: The line regex accepts a bold label (colon either side) and strips backticks.
ambiguities.why: The handoff strips * and ` from the text after Status:, but the colon sits inside the bold in '**Status:**'. The line regex must allow ** around 'Status:' and the colon either side.
ambiguities.was: parser must accept the bold label and strip backticks

ambiguities.case: ranges '03–07' (en dash) and '03-07' (hyphen)
ambiguities.chosen: Both en dash and hyphen ranges are expanded inclusively, start <= end, no existence check.
ambiguities.why: Handoff names only the en dash. A hyphen could also appear in a slug. Expansion does not check that the numbers exist in the space (09 gets 03,04,05,06,07; 03-07 spans folders).
ambiguities.was: both are ranges, expanded inclusively to every number from start to end

ambiguities.case: mixed '01, 03–05' (ticket 100); free text with a leading number '05 (only the ADO part)' (issue 26); 'none' and '—'
ambiguities.chosen: A comma list of numbers and ranges gives refs (100: 01, 03, 04, 05). A number followed by words (26) is free text: blocked_by [] and blocked_note holds the raw text. none, dash, n/a and empty give [] and no note.
ambiguities.why: 'Refs are pulled out only when it is bare numbers'. A comma list mixing numbers and ranges is still bare numbers. A number followed by words is not, so the ref is lost. The parser might also salvage the leading number; not done here.
ambiguities.was: mixed list: refs 01,03,04,05. Number plus text: free text, blocked_by [], blocked_note holds the raw line. none, —, empty, n/a: [] and no note

ambiguities.case: free text like 'waiting for the DBA...' or 'client answers'
ambiguities.chosen: Free text gives blocked_by [] and blocked_note = raw text.
ambiguities.why: Per section 3. The blocked_note is stored for any non-empty, non-ref text, including 'none' variants when written as prose.

ambiguities.case: ticket numbers of 3 digits and 5+ digits
ambiguities.chosen: num is kept as written; key and refs use pad2(parseInt(num)).
ambiguities.why: Section 1: 5, 05 and 005 are the same ticket, and two digits minimum.
ambiguities.was: num keeps the file's digits as written ('100'); refs pad to at least 2 digits

ambiguities.case: one-cash-mover is mixed: 01 and 06 legacy, 05 migrated
ambiguities.chosen: legacy is decided per file, never per space.
ambiguities.why: A space can hold both. The viewer must not decide per space.
ambiguities.was: legacy is decided per file, by the absence of frontmatter

ambiguities.case: Label line (wayfinder:bug)
ambiguities.chosen: Label: is not mapped into meta; it stays body text.
ambiguities.why: Section 3 gives no mapping for Label. It is kept as plain body text.

ambiguities.case: issues/02 and 26 have no number in the H1
ambiguities.chosen: num always comes from the filename; title is the H1 minus an optional leading "NN — ".
ambiguities.why: Section 1.
ambiguities.was: num always comes from the filename, never the H1

ambiguities.case: every legacy file with a Status line
ambiguities.chosen: status_note is stripped (* ` ✅ removed, quotes normalised, trimmed); null when empty. Every record carries it.
ambiguities.why: Section 3 says the original text becomes status_note but does not say whether it is the stripped or raw text.
ambiguities.was: status_note is the text after Status: with * ` ✅ stripped and trimmed (null when empty)

ambiguities.case: remove-service-account issues/10 blocked_by "cloud-migration 07#q3"
ambiguities.chosen: the only intentionally dangling ref: cloud-migration issues/07 has no q3 anchor (only an unanchored Q1 heading). The ref "one-cash-mover#q3" in issues/07 resolves, because one-cash-mover/map.md now has anchor q3.
ambiguities.why: Gives the checker and viewer one unresolved item-ref to handle.
